scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service subscription canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Julio Perez and I'm 43. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Julio, thank you for reaching out. I understand how frustrating it can be to return from travel and find unexpected charges. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide the email address associated with your account and the last four digits of the payment card used?
Sure, the email is jperez81@email.com and the card ends in 4492.

Thank you, Julio. I have located your account. I can see the cancellation was processed on day 34 of your billing cycle. Our 'Service Terms & Refund Policy' (Section 4.2) typically limits full refunds to requests made within 30 days of the renewal charge. However, since you have been a loyal customer for two years, I can submit a one-time exception request for you.
That would be incredibly helpful, thank you. I really didn't use the service at all during that time.

You're very welcome. I have reviewed your account activity, and I can confirm there was no usage of the platform during this period. I have successfully processed the refund of $49.99 to your card ending in 4492. You should see the funds reflected in your account within 3-5 business days depending on your bank.
That is great news. I really appreciate you working with me on this, despite being slightly past the window.
It was my pleasure, Julio. I'm glad we could resolve this for you today. Is there anything else I can assist you with?

resolution_summary: Agent verified account ownership and usage history, then applied a one-time policy exception for a loyal customer to issue a full refund despite the request falling outside the 30-day window.

judge_scores.justification: The agent verified account ownership appropriately and demonstrated strong empathy by acknowledging the customer's travel situation. Furthermore, the agent efficiently resolved the issue within their authority by citing specific policy (Section 4.2) and granting a well-reasoned one-time exception based on account history and lack of usage.
